sections.label: Election deposit based on MP allowance
sections.summary: The election deposit will be based on an elected MP's fixed monthly allowance, rounded to the nearest $500.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The election deposit will now be based on an elected Member of Parliament's fixed monthly allowance, rounded to the nearest $500.

sections.label: Election expense supporting documents
sections.summary: Clause 23 removes the requirement for election agents to submit supporting documents, while clause 25 requires candidates and agents to keep them for one year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Clause 23 amends section 74 to remove the current requirement for election agents to submit to the Returning Officer the supporting documents for election expenses, such as bills and receipts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: To ensure accountability, clause 25 inserts a new section 75A to require a candidate and the candidate's election agent to maintain the supporting documents for the return on election expenses for a period of one year after notice of the return is published by the Returning Officer in the Government Gazette.

sections.label: Returning Officer keeping election returns
sections.summary: The clause extends the period the Returning Officer must keep returns and statements on election expenses from six months to one year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The clause also extends the period of time for which the Returning Officer must keep the returns and statements on election expenses from the current six months to one year.

sections.label: Suspension of nomination proceedings
sections.summary: Before deciding under new section 56BA(3), the Returning Officer may suspend nomination proceedings for up to two hours to assess the situation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Before making a decision under the new section 56BA(3), the Returning Officer may suspend the nomination proceedings for a period of up to two hours in order to assess the situation and decide on the course of actions to be taken.

sections.label: Rejecting claims without public inquiry
sections.summary: Clause 3 lets the Registration Officer reject clearly meritless claims without a public inquiry, with grounds scoped in new section 11(9B).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Clause 3 amends section 11 to enable the Registration Officer to reject, without having to hold a public inquiry, a claim for a name to be included in a Register of Electors for an electoral division if the claim is clearly without merit.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: To safeguard claimants' interests, the grounds on which the Registration Officer may reject a claim without holding a public inquiry are tightly scoped in the new section 11(9B) as follows: (a) the claimant was not a citizen of Singapore on the relevant cut-off date for the Register; (b) the claimant was below 21 years of age on the relevant cut-off date; (c) where the claimant claims to be entitled to be included in the Register on the ground that the claimant's address has changed, the new address provided by the claimant is not the address of any premises within the electoral division, such as a P O (post office) box address.

sections.label: Number of NCMPs declared
sections.summary: Clause 16 increases the number of NCMPs to be declared to 12 minus the total number of elected Opposition Members of Parliament.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Lastly, consequential to amendments made in 2016 to the Constitution, clause 16 amends section 52 to increase the number of Non-Constituency Members of Parliament (NCMPs) to be declared.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The clause increases the number of NCMPs to be declared to 12 minus the total number of elected Opposition Members of Parliament.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The amendments I have described today will improve the administration of Parliamentary elections while ensuring the secrecy of the vote and the integrity of the election process.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The changes will ensure that our electorate continues to have high trust and confidence in our electoral system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: I have seen a ballot paper with a faint squiggly cross marked inside the demarcated box rejected by an Assistant Returning Officer (ARO) on the basis that the intention of the voter was not clear.

sections.label: Returning Officer on rejected votes
sections.summary: The Returning Officer said the individual ARO at each counting table has authority to decide on rejected votes' validity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: When I asked the Returning Officer to adjudicate on the validity of the rejected votes, he said the individual ARO at the respective counting tables has the authority to decide on such a matter.

sections.label: Clause 11 ballot paper mark
sections.summary: Clause 11 introduces a sub-section requiring the voter's mark to be made in the demarcated area, not elsewhere.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: First, clause 11 of this Bill, which amends section 42 of the Parliamentary Elections Act, introduces a new sub-section (3AA), which states that “the voter’s mark on the ballot paper must be made in the area demarcated on the ballot paper for that purpose, and not elsewhere.” Sir, to the visually impaired or elderly with poor eyesight, putting a mark squarely within the area demarcated on the ballot paper can be challenging, especially if these voters do not want any help to do so for whatever reason.

sections.label: Opposition to NCMP scheme
sections.summary: The speaker opposes the NCMP scheme but supports the Bill apart from the amendment revising the NCMP number formula.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: We oppose the scheme as we believe in the fundamental principle that having more NCMPs is not the way forward to make our political system more robust.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: So, barring the amendment made to section 52(1) of the principal Act to revise the formula to determine the number of NCMP to be declared in an election, I do support the amendment Bill.

sections.label: Rejection of claims without hearing
sections.summary: New section 11(9B)(b) allows rejection of eligibility claims without hearing on citizenship, age or address grounds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The new section 11(9B)(b) allows rejections of claims for eligibility without hearing, if the Registration Officer is satisfied that the claimant was not a citizen of Singapore or below 21 on the date prescribed in section 5(4), or the claimant's new address in the claim form is not in the relevant electoral division.

sections.label: Lost or destroyed ballot boxes
sections.summary: New section 56DA abandons counting and restarts the poll if a ballot box is lost or destroyed and material to the result.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Under the new section 56DA, if any ballot box containing votes cast is lost or destroyed, the counting of all votes cast at the affected polling station will be abandoned and the poll at that polling station must be restarted only if it is material to the election result.

sections.label: Clause 3 rejection of claims
sections.summary: Clause 3's new section 9B(b) allows rejection of eligibility claims without hearing on citizenship, age or address grounds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Clause 3 provides for a new section 9B(b) which allows for rejection of claim for eligibility without hearing if the Registration Officer is satisfied that the claimant was not a citizen of Singapore or below 21 at the date prescribed in section 5(4) and the claimant's new address in the claim form is not in an electoral division.

sections.label: Returning Officers ballot mark disputes
sections.summary: The Government should review and strengthen how Returning Officers handle disagreements over the validity of a voter's mark on a ballot.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Government should also review and strengthen the process by which Returning Officers handle any disagreement by candidates or their representatives, their counting agents, in respect of the validity of a voter's mark in a ballot to enhance certainty and transparency.

sections.label: Electoral division changes published online
sections.summary: Clause 2 proposes that changes in electoral divisions may be published as maps online or for public viewing instead of in the Gazette.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Clause 2 proposes that changes in electoral divisions may be published as maps online or for public viewing, instead of in written detail in the Gazette.

sections.label: One lost ballot box counting
sections.summary: Clause 19 proposes that if just one ballot box is lost or destroyed from a polling station, all counting from that station must be abandoned.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Clause 19 proposes that if just one ballot box is lost or destroyed from a polling station, then all counting of votes from that polling station must be abandoned.

sections.label: Re-polling margins in past elections
sections.summary: Calculations show the 2011 GE had two SMCs and the 2015 GE two SMCs and one GRC with margins requiring re-polling.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, I did some calculations for the last two GEs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It turns out that in the 2011 GE, the margin of victory was slim enough in two Single Member Constituencies (SMCs) that they would have required re-polling.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the 2015 GE, it was two SMCs and one Group Representation Constituency (GRC) which would have required re-polling.

sections.label: Clause 19 Minister reserve powers
sections.summary: Clause 19 reserves powers to the Minister over procedures, and the speaker suggests giving them to the Returning Officer instead.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The last point I want to make is that clause 19 also does reserve powers to the Minister to decide how these procedures are to be carried out.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: When Parliament is dissolved, the incumbent Cabinet does hold office until the first Sitting of the new Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, the Minister's ability to form the Government may well depend on the outcome of this single polling station.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In another country, the results of a recent general election were unclear until well past the midnight hour.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, I would suggest we consider reserving these powers to the Returning Officer to avoid any appearance of partiality.

sections.label: Candidate deposits payment methods
sections.summary: Clause 4(e) proposes that candidate deposits be made by electronic funds transfer, bank draft, or certified cheque.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The first one, Mr Speaker, Sir, is in relation to deposits by candidates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I note that under clause 4(e) of the Bill, it is proposed that the deposit must be made through electronic funds transfer system, or bank draft, or certified cheque.

sections.label: Recount at 2% margin
sections.summary: Clause 14 requires the Returning Officer to conduct a recount when the vote difference is 2% or less.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Second, on the recounting of votes, I note that clause 14 of the Bill provides that the Returning Officer must conduct a recount where the difference between candidates with the most number of votes, and the next candidate is 2% or less.

sections.label: Clause 25 supporting documents
sections.summary: Clause 25 proposes a system where a candidate does not have to provide supporting documents such as bills and receipts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Clause 25 proposes a different system where a candidate does not have to provide supporting documents, meaning bills and receipts.

sections.label: Loss of documents feared
sections.summary: The speaker fears unintended consequences such as loss of documents during the one-year holding period for candidates or election agents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Under the proposed system, I fear that there could be unintended consequences, for example, loss of documents during the one-year period that the candidate or the election agent is supposed to hold on to these documents.

sections.label: Re-voting only if decisive
sections.summary: The speaker suggests re-voting should be held only if votes in affected boxes could potentially sway the election result.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Perhaps it would be better that the re-voting exercise be held only in the event that the votes in the affected boxes could potentially sway the election result.

sections.label: Election deposit based on allowance
sections.summary: An amendment bases the election deposit on an elected MP's monthly allowance, rounded to the nearest $500, and asks if PMO will reduce it further.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: One of the amendments is that elections deposit will be based on an elected Member of Parliament's monthly allowance, rounded to the nearest $500.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Will the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) consider reducing the deposit required further, such as by pegging against the median gross monthly income for full-time work, which is currently $4,232?

sections.label: Automating nomination forms
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Elections Department will further automate nomination forms to be largely system-enabled for nominees, proposers and seconders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Will the Elections Department consider further automating the nomination forms to make it largely system-enabled for potential nominees/candidates as well as for proposers and seconders?

sections.label: MP allowance election deposit rate
sections.summary: Setting the deposit at one month of a Member of Parliament's allowance has worked reasonably well since Singapore's first elections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Setting at the current rate of one month of a Member of Parliament’s allowance has worked reasonably well since we first had elections in Singapore.

sections.label: Fresh polls on affected votes
sections.summary: Fresh polls will be conducted if the number of votes affects the election results for the electoral division.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Fresh polls will be conducted if the number of votes affects the election results for the electoral division.

sections.label: Contingency procedure for Parliamentary elections
sections.summary: A contingency procedure for affected votes, already used in Presidential elections, is proposed to apply to Parliamentary elections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: And how do we know whether the affected votes might affect the election results?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: This is when the sum of the total number of affected voters and the total number of overseas voters from the affected electoral division are equal or more than the difference between the votes already counted for the top two candidates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: This contingency procedure has been in place for Presidential elections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Now, what is new is the proposal to apply the same contingency procedures to Parliamentary elections as well.

sections.label: Returning Officer procedures for lost ballot boxes
sections.summary: New section 56DA sets out Returning Officer procedures when a ballot box is lost or destroyed after polls close in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira asked if providing the Minister with powers to decide how a re-poll is to be done will be a conflict of interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Now, let me assure Members that the new section 56DA spells out clearly the procedures to be undertaken by the Returning Officer when a ballot box is lost or destroyed after the close of polls in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: This includes informing the candidates of the affected electoral division, publishing a notice in the Gazette that the Returning Officer has abandoned the counting of the votes cast at the affected polling station and, if there is a need for a fresh poll, to specify the date, hours of the poll and location of the polling station.

sections.label: Ballot box custody chain
sections.summary: A rigorous process ensures no break in the chain of custody of ballot boxes from polling stations to counting centres to the Supreme Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh also asked if there had been previous cases of tampering with ballot boxes during an election.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: There is a rigorous process to ensure that there is no break in the chain of custody of the ballot boxes from the polling stations to the counting centres, and from the counting centres to the Supreme Court where the ballot papers are retained in safe custody for a period of time before they are subsequently destroyed.

sections.label: Overseas votes custody and election officials
sections.summary: Overseas ballot boxes have a secured chain of custody, and elections are administered by trained public officers impartially and transparently.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: For overseas votes, there is similarly a secured chain of custody.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Sealed ballot boxes are transported back to Singapore by two election officials and they are kept at the Supreme Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: After counting, the ballot boxes are then transported back to the Supreme Court to be kept together with the local ballot boxes for six months before they are destroyed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: On Mr Gan Thiam Poh’s and Mr Png Eng Huat’s comments on election officials, let me first emphasise that the elections are administered by public officers who have been trained to do their election duties according to the law, in an impartial and transparent fashion.

sections.label: Maps kept with National Archives
sections.summary: The maps would be kept with the National Archives in due course, as with other public records.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: As with other public records, the maps would also be kept with the National Archives in due course.

sections.label: Deposit payment methods amendment
sections.summary: The old section 28(2) deposit payment wording is deleted and replaced by a new provision allowing electronic funds transfer, bank draft, certified cheque or other forms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: I just want to point out that in relation to the amendment Bill, under the old section 28(2), it reads the deposit may be paid but "Any sum required to be deposited under subsection (1) shall be paid in legal tender or by a bank draft or a certified cheque".

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: That has been deleted and replaced by the new proposed provision, which reads "The deposit of the sum required under sub-section (1) must be made through an electronic funds transfer system designated by the Returning Officer for that purpose, or by a bank draft or a certified cheque, or in such other form or manner as the Returning Officer allows".

sections.label: Member's interpretation confirmed
sections.summary: The answer is yes and the Member's interpretation is correct.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The answer is yes, the Member's interpretation is correct.

sections.label: Cash acceptance by Returning Officer
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister to indicate the Returning Officer should accept cash, and says cash can be accepted in extenuating circumstances when electronic payment fails.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: So, I would ask the Minister to give some indication that the Returning Officer should accept cash, unless there is a very good reason why – and I cannot think of any – why cash should not be accepted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: But in extenuating circumstances, as the Member has mentioned whereby the electronic payment system failed, then we are able to accept cash.

sections.label: Ballot paper layout improvements
sections.summary: With today's amendments it will be clearer because the ballot paper layout is improved with black contrasted against white and white marking boxes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: There is nothing that we need to hide.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: So, with today's amendments, it will be even clearer because, first, we have improved on the layout of the ballot paper, where it is black contrasted with white, and the white boxes where people are supposed to mark are clearly contrasted against all the other areas that are printed in black.
